raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill / extend rows run wo_a (`o [T, G, 4096] @ wo_a [G, 1024, 4096]`; G = 4 at TP2, 2 at TP4, 8 at DP-attn) as `torch.einsum`. Only TP4 with 4096-65536 rows uses a strided `torch.bmm`. The einsum hands back its group-major result as a `[T, G, R]` view, so wo_b's `flatten(1)` copies it. wo_b (gfx950 MXFP8 route) then quantizes the bf16 copy in a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` pass, whose 64x32 tiles drop to about 2.2 TB/s once the input no longer fits in the cache. Decode / verify rows at TP2 / DP-attn already get wo_b's `Mxfp8Activation` from the wo_a GEMM epilogue (#42055).

At TP2, a 16K-row layer spends 608 us in wo_a: einsum 450 us, flatten copy about 105 us, quant about 46 us. Layers 0-20 of every 16K chunk see all rows. Layers 21-39 see 128 rows per request under decoder SWA bounded replay.

Moving the epilogue route (the Triton fork `gfx95_batched_gemm_bf16_fp8_grid`, `emit_fp8`) to prefill sizes does not pay off. I swept tile sizes, warps, `waves_per_eu`, stages, and an XCD remap with grouped tile order under the production Triton env (`TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0`). The best tile reaches about 825 TFLOP/s against hipBLASLt's about 1250. Even with the quant fused, it is 7-11% slower than today at TP2 for 4K+ rows and 18-32% slower at TP4. So this PR keeps hipBLASLt and drops the copy and the slow quant instead.

## Modifications

- `_apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul`: on V4.1 gfx950, prefill / extend rows of every local group count and row count go to `wo_a_prefill_matmul` (`deepseek_v4_gfx95_dense`):
  - `torch.bmm` writes the token-major `[T, G, R]` directly, the strided destination TP4 already uses for 4096-65536 rows. wo_b's `flatten(1)` becomes a view, and the result is bitwise the einsum's.
  - When wo_b consumes MXFP8 (`wo_b_emits_mxfp8` / `SGLANG_HIP_WO_A_MXFP8`, the decode gate), one `fp8_grid_quantize` pass (32x512 tiles) returns wo_b's `Mxfp8Activation` instead of wo_b quantizing the bf16 tensor itself. Its fp8 codes and ue8m0 scales equal wo_b's own quant for every 32-group with amax >= 1e-10; this was checked over all bf16 amax values. An all-zero group keeps its zero codes under a different exponent (85 vs 19), as in the decode epilogue.
  - Batch-invariant and deterministic inference keep the einsum.
- Decode / target-verify branches are unchanged.
- `test_deepseek_v4_amd_wo_a_bf16.py`: G = 2 / 4 / 8 at 1-16384 rows (bitwise vs the einsum; MXFP8 bytes vs `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, including an all-zero row), CUDA-graph replay, batch-invariant fallback, DSv4 keeps the einsum.

## Accuracy Tests

- The unit tests above pass on MI355X. Per layer, wo_b's output (aiter MXFP8 GEMM) is bitwise equal to today's at G = 2 / 4 / 8 and 128-16384 rows.
- GSM8K (1319 questions, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP2, DSpark): base 0.893 / 0.891, this PR 0.903 / 0.902 (two runs per arm; the server is run-to-run nondeterministic).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X x1, `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261018`, CUDA-graph replay (median), `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0 TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1`. wo_a plus its quant for wo_b, us (before → after):

| rows | TP2 (G = 4) | TP4 (G = 2) | DP-attn (G = 8) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 22.8 → 17.9 | 17.1 → 12.7 | 33.9 → 27.9 |
| 1024 | 76.5 → 66.4 | 41.3 → 35.0 | 88.0 → 71.8 |
| 2048 | 84.8 → 68.3 | 77.0 → 66.2 | 155.7 → 125.6 |
| 4096 | 147.7 → 123.4 | 72.0 → 71.4 | 315.7 → 260.7 |
| 16384 | 607.8 → 488.0 | 270.3 → 257.8 | 1272.5 → 1008.6 |

Including wo_b's GEMM, a TP2 16K-row layer goes from 1048 to 933 us. Per 16K chunk of one request (layers 0-20 at 16384 rows, 21-39 at 128 rows), that is TP2 −2.6 ms, TP4 −0.3 ms, DP-attn −5.7 ms per rank.

End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X x2 (TP2, the same two GPUs one after the other, interleaved base, PR, base, PR), DSpark, production recipe env with `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL=true`, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --prefill-decode-interval 32 --swa-prefix-tails 2048`:

| | base (run 1 / 2) | this PR (run 1 / 2) |
|---|---:|---:|
| prefill TTFT, 16384 in / 1 out, c1, 24 prompts, median | 358.8 / 361.7 ms | 355.8 / 360.8 ms |
| prefill TTFT, p90 | 366.0 / 371.5 ms | 366.8 / 368.1 ms |
| decode 1024 / 1024 c4, median ITL | 2.07 / 2.06 ms | 2.06 / 2.08 ms |
| decode 1024 / 1024 c32, median ITL | 5.09 / 5.06 ms | 5.05 / 5.09 ms |

Averaged over the two runs, the median TTFT is 2.0 ms (0.55%) lower, in line with the −2.6 ms per-chunk estimate from the kernel timings but within the 3-5 ms run-to-run spread. Decode is untouched (median ITL unchanged). The first base run, the first server on a freshly allocated node, has decode TPOT and TTFT stalls the other runs did not have (c4 p90 TPOT 5.56 vs 3.77 ms), so TPOT and throughput are not compared.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import (
     Fp8GridActivation,
     Mxfp8Activation,
+    fp8_grid_quantize,
 )
 from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95 import (
     rmsnorm_fake_quant_fp8,
 )
+from sglang.srt.batch_invariant_ops import is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled
 from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.base_config import QuantizationConfig
 from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config, Fp8LinearMethod
@@ -255,3 +257,26 @@ def wo_a_fp8_grid_matmul(
     if fp8_grid:
         return Fp8GridActivation(y)
     return y.view(o.shape[0], wo_a.shape[0], wo_a.shape[1])
+
+
+def wo_a_prefill_matmul(o: torch.Tensor, wo_a: torch.Tensor, emit_fp8: bool = False):
+    """Prefill / extend rows of o [T, G, D] @ wo_a [G, R, D]^T: hipBLASLt's bmm writes the
+    token-major [T, G, R] wo_b reads (the einsum's group-major result costs wo_b a flatten
+    copy), bitwise the einsum's; with emit_fp8 one fp8_grid_quantize pass then hands wo_b its
+    Mxfp8Activation in place of wo_b's own quant. None keeps batch-invariant and deterministic
+    inference on the einsum."""
+    if (
+        is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+        or get_exec().deterministic.enable_deterministic_inference
+        or not (o.dtype == wo_a.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and o.stride(2) == 1)
+    ):
+        return None
+    T, G, _ = o.shape
+    R = wo_a.shape[1]
+    y = torch.empty((T, G, R), dtype=o.dtype, device=o.device)
+    # draft warmup / capture can enter with grad enabled
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        torch.bmm(o.transpose(0, 1), wo_a.transpose(1, 2), out=y.transpose(0, 1))
+    if emit_fp8:
+        return Mxfp8Activation(*fp8_grid_quantize(y.view(T, G * R)))
+    return y

@@ -300,5 +300,110 @@ def test_dsv4_keeps_the_main_routes(self):
                     )
 
 
+@unittest.skipUnless(is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported(), "requires gfx950")
+class TestWoAPrefillTokenMajorMxfp8(unittest.TestCase):
+    """gfx950 prefill / extend rows at every local group count (TP4 2, TP2 4, DP-attn 8):
+    the token-major bmm is bitwise the einsum and the MXFP8 hand-off is wo_b's own quant."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_v4 import _apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul
+        from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
+
+        override = get_context().override_server_args()
+        override.install()
+        self.addCleanup(override.restore)
+        self.project = functools.partial(
+            _apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul, fast_path=True, is_decode=False, is_prefill=True
+        )
+        torch.manual_seed(1024)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def operands(rows, groups):
+        x = torch.randn(rows, groups, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        w = torch.randn(groups, 1024, 4096, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        return x, w * 0.015625
+
+    def test_bf16_and_mxfp8_match_einsum_and_wo_b_quant(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import (
+            Mxfp8Activation,
+            dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16,
+            mxfp8_e4m3_quantize,
+        )
+
+        for groups, rows in (
+            (2, 128),
+            (2, 2048),
+            (4, 1),
+            (4, 1000),
+            (4, 16384),
+            (8, 1024),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(groups=groups, rows=rows):
+                x, w = self.operands(rows, groups)
+                # an all-zero row: its groups keep their zero codes under another exponent
+                x[-1].zero_()
+                ref = torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", x, w)
+                y = self.project(x, w)
+                self.assertTrue(y.is_contiguous())
+                torch.testing.assert_close(y, ref, atol=0, rtol=0)
+                act = self.project(x, w, emit_fp8=True)
+                self.assertIsInstance(act, Mxfp8Activation)
+                q, scale = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(ref.flatten(1))
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(act.q.view(torch.uint8), q.view(torch.uint8))
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(act.scale[:-1], scale[:-1]))
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(
+                        dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(act.q, act.scale),
+                        dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(q, scale),
+                    )
+                )
+
+    def test_mxfp8_under_graph_replay(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import mxfp8_e4m3_quantize
+
+        x, w = self.operands(4096, 4)
+        self.project(x, w, emit_fp8=True)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            act = self.project(x, w, emit_fp8=True)
+        for _ in range(2):
+            x.normal_()
+            w.normal_(std=0.015625)
+            graph.replay()
+            ref = torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", x, w).flatten(1)
+            q, scale = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(ref)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(act.q.view(torch.uint8), q.view(torch.uint8)))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(act.scale, scale))
+
+    def test_dsv4_keeps_the_einsum(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models import deepseek_v4 as dsv4
+
+        taken = mock.Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("DSv4 took a V4.1 gfx950 route"))
+        x, w = self.operands(1024, 4)
+        with mock.patch.object(dsv4._hip, "wo_a_prefill_matmul", taken):
+            y = dsv4._apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul(x, w, is_decode=False, is_prefill=True)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            y, torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", x, w), atol=0, rtol=0
+        )
+
+    def test_batch_invariant_keeps_the_einsum(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_common.amd import (
+            deepseek_v4_gfx95_dense as gfx95_dense,
+        )
+
+        x, w = self.operands(1024, 4)
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            gfx95_dense, "is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled", return_value=True
+        ):
+            self.assertIsNone(gfx95_dense.wo_a_prefill_matmul(x, w, emit_fp8=True))
+            y = self.project(x, w, emit_fp8=True)
+        self.assertIsInstance(y, torch.Tensor)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            y, torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", x, w), atol=0, rtol=0
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
